arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Bennett argued federal courts have deferentially reviewed legislation affecting property for seventy years.
Mr. Kneedler stated the rational basis standard goes to the heart of the judicial role.
Mr. Stewart identified the issue as the content of the regulatory takings doctrine.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the standard for reviewing economic regulations that affect property rights. the sides that brought the case argue for a higher level of scrutiny. the opposing sides support the existing rational basis test.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the Court to adopt the substantially advances test for regulatory takings claims.
the opposing sides want the Court to maintain the rational basis standard for reviewing economic legislation.
